One Channel Is Carrying You, and It Isn't Yours.

Analysislowob research

By lowob · 24 June 2026 · 7-minute read · Distribution

In short: The most dangerous distribution position is not being invisible. It is being visible on one channel that someone else controls. Platforms change rules, ranking systems and features on their own dates: Meta removed lookalike audiences for US financial ads in January 2025, Google cut low-quality results in search by 45% in 2024, and Pew found users clicked a result about half as often on Google searches that showed an AI summary. Price the dependency with three numbers, build a second channel with a different failure mode while the first one still pays for it, and keep no channel above half of outcomes for more than two quarters.

Key points

  • Concentration is what early success looks like; the mistake is not starting the next measurement once the first channel works.
  • Channel owners change terms on their own timetable, with dated announcements and enforcement windows measured in weeks.
  • Three numbers price the risk: share of outcomes from the largest channel, weeks to replace it, and the cost of the gap.
  • Alternatives should fail for different reasons: partners choose to carry you, and no reviewer can un-choose them.
  • Rule of thumb: no channel above half of outcomes for more than two quarters.

The company is working. Accounts are opening, subscriptions are starting, the cost per outcome is acceptable. Almost all of it comes from one place: one ad platform, one app store, one creator, one search engine, one marketplace. The dashboard is green, and the board is relaxed.

Then a policy changes on a Tuesday. A category is reclassified. An algorithm is adjusted. A creator moves on. An app-store review is reversed. The channel does not fail slowly. It stops.

The channel owner sets the calendar

This is not a hypothetical risk. The large channels publish their changes, and the dates are theirs.

DateChannelWhat changedWho it hit
March to April 2024Google SearchA core update and new spam policies; Google reported 45% less low-quality, unoriginal content in results once the rollout finished on 19 April 2024Publishers and sites relying on search traffic
January 2025Meta adsFinancial products and services ads to US audiences required to run in a special ad category; lookalike audiences unavailable; some customer-list audiences ineligible from March 2025Fintechs whose acquisition ran on lookalikes
March 2025 data, published July 2025Google SearchPew found users clicked a result on 8% of visits with an AI summary, against 15% withoutAny business whose content depended on the click
June to July 2026Google AdsFinancial services verification extended to 24 EEA markets; advertisers that do not complete it by their enforcement date lose the ability to show financial services ads thereFinancial advertisers in those markets
OngoingApple App StoreApple describes its review guidelines as "a living document" where "new apps presenting new questions may result in new rules at any time"Any app-dependent business

None of these was a failure of the companies affected. Each was a reasonable decision by a channel owner pursuing its own goals. That is the point: a channel you do not own will always be run for someone else's reasons.

Why it happens to good companies

Concentration is what success looks like when it is early.

A channel reads, and the sensible thing is to put everything behind it. That is correct, and we would advise it. The mistake is not the commitment; it is forgetting to start the next measurement once the commitment is made. The company that found its first channel in month three is still on it alone in month eighteen, because it worked, and nobody wanted to spend money learning something they did not need to know yet.

In categories the platforms review, the risk is sharper, because the channel carrying the company is often one that tolerates the category rather than welcomes it. Tolerance is revoked more easily than approval. Our explainer on what a restricted category is covers how platforms make that call.

Tolerance is revoked more easily than approval.

Price the risk before it is priced for you

Three numbers turn a vague worry into a decision.

Share of outcomes from the largest channel. Above half, the company has a dependency. Above three quarters, it has a single point of failure with a marketing department attached.

Time to replace. If the channel stopped today, how many weeks until an alternative could carry even half the volume? For a company with nothing else built, the honest answer is often a quarter or more.

Cost of the gap. Weekly outcomes from the channel, multiplied by the weeks to replace, multiplied by the value of an outcome. That figure is what the dependency is worth, and it is usually large enough to justify building the alternative now.

InputIllustrative figure
Outcomes per week from the largest channel400 funded accounts
Share of all outcomes80%
Weeks to replace half the volume with nothing else built13
Value of an outcome (contribution over first year)$120
Cost of the gap: 400 × 13 × $120$624,000

Illustrative arithmetic, not a client figure. Use your own contribution value, not revenue.

Set that figure beside the cost of standing up a second channel at modest scale for two quarters; that comparison is the decision. Demand generation economics covers how to value an outcome so the calculation holds up with finance.

Build the second channel while the first one is still working

The counterintuitive part is timing. The right moment to stand up the second channel is when the company can least see the need for it: when the first one is performing and the budget seems better spent there.

That is because a second channel takes time nobody has once the first one fails. An affiliate programme needs terms, partner recruitment, tracking and a few months of history before it carries real volume. A creator programme needs relationships. A programmatic buy needs inventory standards and a learning period. All of that can be built at modest cost while the main channel pays for it. None of it can be built in the two weeks after an account is suspended.

What the alternatives look like

The point is not to abandon the channel that works. It is to add channels with different failure modes.

Dependent onAddWhy it fails differently
One ad platformAn affiliate and partner programmePartners choose to carry a product, and no reviewer can un-choose it for them
One creatorA second tier of smaller creators in a structured programmeNo single relationship carries the category
SearchOwned email and contentNo ranking update can remove a list you own
One marketplaceDirect distributionThe customer relationship sits with you, not the platform
One partnerA second partner of a different typeChannel rules stop one partner's terms becoming yours

Each of these is unglamorous compared with the channel that is working. Each is also thinly bid, for the same reason; our piece on thin bidding makes the case. Partner channel design covers how to set up partner types so they do not compete for the same deals, and channel conflict and how to manage it covers the rules that keep a second channel from cannibalising the first. For software sellers, marketplace listings are a procurement route that can sit beside direct sales rather than replace it.

The rule of thumb

No channel above half of outcomes for more than two quarters. When a channel crosses that line, the next measurement starts, funded from the channel that is working. Report the share of the largest channel to the board alongside cost per outcome, so concentration is visible before it becomes a crisis.

The goal is a small constellation of channels rather than one bright light: individually faint, together recognisable, and still visible when any single one goes out. A channel that works is a reason to start building the next one, not a reason to stop.

lowob takeaways

  • Assume the owner will change the rules. Google, Meta and Apple all did, on dated announcements, in the last three years.
  • Price the dependency in money. Weekly outcomes times weeks to replace times contribution per outcome.
  • Build the second channel early. It takes months to carry volume and can be funded by the first.
  • Choose a different failure mode. Partners, owned lists and direct relationships fail for different reasons.
  • Cap concentration at half. Two quarters above it starts the next measurement.

Common questions

What is single-channel dependency in marketing?

When most of a company's customers come from one channel it does not control, such as one ad platform, app store, search engine, creator or marketplace. A single rule or algorithm change can stop acquisition.

How do you measure channel concentration risk?

Track the share of outcomes from the largest channel, estimate the weeks to replace half its volume, and multiply weekly outcomes by those weeks and by the contribution value of an outcome. That is the cost of the gap.

How many marketing channels should a company have?

Enough that no single channel carries more than half of outcomes for more than two quarters. Two or three working channels with different failure modes are usually sufficient.

When should a startup add a second acquisition channel?

While the first channel is still performing and can fund it. A second channel needs months to carry volume, so it cannot be built after the first one fails.

Sources and notes

  • Google, New updates to address spam and low-quality results, 5 March 2024, updated 26 April 2024. Company announcement; the 45% figure is Google's own measure.
  • Meta for Developers, Out-of-cycle changes 2024, entries dated October 2024 to January 2025. Developer changelog; US-focused.
  • Meta for Developers, Special Ad Categories, checked 16 November 2026. Developer documentation.
  • Pew Research Center, Google users are less likely to click on links when an AI summary appears, 22 July 2025. 900 US adults, consumer searches in March 2025.
  • Google Ads, Introducing new verification requirements for certain financial services advertisers (June 2026), posted 23 June 2026. Covers 24 EEA markets.
  • Apple, App Review Guidelines, checked 16 November 2026. Platform rules.
  • The three numbers, the illustrative calculation and the half-of-outcomes rule are lowob's framework.

Next Move

Calculate your three numbers this week: the largest channel's share of outcomes, your honest weeks to replace half of it, and the cost of the gap. If the share is above half, scope a second channel with a different failure mode and fund its first quarter from the channel that is working.
